npc.ar: أَهْلًا وَسَهْلًا يَا فَيْصَل! تَفَضَّلْ، الْبَيْت بَيْتُكَ.
npc.en: Welcome, Faisal! Please come in and make yourself at home.

choices.ar: شُكْرًا يَا أُسْتَاذ أَحْمَد. هٰذِهِ حَلَوِيَّات لَكُمْ.
choices.en: Thank you, Mr Ahmad. These sweets are for you.
choices.feedback: Good: a small gift of sweets is the custom, and لَكُمْ (for you, plural) gives it to the whole family.

choices.ar: شُكْرًا يَا أُسْتَاذ أَحْمَد. هٰذَا حَلَوِيَّات لَكُمْ.
choices.en: Thank you, Mr Ahmad. These sweets are for you (wrong form of 'this').
choices.feedback: حَلَوِيَّات is a plural of things, and such plurals take feminine singular words: هٰذِهِ حَلَوِيَّات، not هٰذَا.

npc.ar: أَهْلًا يَا فَيْصَل! مَاذَا تَشْرَبُ؟ عِنْدَنَا شَاي وَقَهْوَة وَعَصِير.
npc.en: Hello, Faisal! What would you like to drink? We have tea, coffee and juice.

choices.ar: شَاي، مِنْ فَضْلِكِ، بِدُونِ سُكَّر. بَيْتُكُمْ جَمِيل جِدًّا!
choices.en: Tea, please, without sugar. Your home is very beautiful!
choices.feedback: Good: مِنْ فَضْلِكِ (-ki) to Dr Fatima, and بَيْتُكُمْ (-kum) because the home belongs to the whole family.

choices.ar: قَهْوَة، مِنْ فَضْلِكِ، بِدُونِ سُكَّر. بَيْتُكُمْ جَمِيل جِدًّا!
choices.en: Coffee, please, without sugar. Your home is very beautiful!
choices.feedback: Good: coffee instead of tea, with -ki to Dr Fatima and a compliment for the home.

choices.ar: شَاي، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ، بِدُونِ سُكَّر. بَيْتُكُمْ جَمِيل جِدًّا!
choices.en: Tea, please, without sugar. Your home is very beautiful! (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: مِنْ فَضْلِكَ (-ka) is for a man. Dr Fatima is a woman: مِنْ فَضْلِكِ (-ki).

npc.ar: تَفَضَّلِ الشَّاي، وَخُذْ قِطْعَةَ كَعْك أُخْرَى!
npc.en: Here's your tea, and have another piece of cake!

choices.ar: شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا، الْكَعْك لَذِيذ، لٰكِنْ يَكْفِي، أَنَا شَبْعَان!
choices.en: Thank you so much, the cake is delicious, but that's enough, I'm full!
choices.feedback: Polite and clear: praise the food first, then يَكْفِي (that's enough) when you are really full.

choices.ar: شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا، الْكَعْك لَذِيذَة، لٰكِنْ يَكْفِي، أَنَا شَبْعَان!
choices.en: Thank you so much, the cake is delicious, but that's enough, I'm full! (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: كَعْك is masculine, so the adjective has no ة: الْكَعْك لَذِيذ.

npc.ar: تَفَضَّلِ الْقَهْوَة، وَخُذْ قِطْعَةَ كَعْك أُخْرَى!
npc.en: Here's your coffee, and have another piece of cake!

choices.ar: شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا، الْكَعْك لَذِيذ، لٰكِنْ يَكْفِي، أَنَا شَبْعَان!
choices.en: Thank you so much, the cake is delicious, but that's enough, I'm full!
choices.feedback: Polite and clear: praise the food first, then يَكْفِي (that's enough) when you are really full.

choices.ar: شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا، الْكَعْك لَذِيذ، لٰكِنْ يَكْفِي، أَنْتَ شَبْعَان!
choices.en: Thank you so much, the cake is delicious, but that's enough, you're full! (wrong word)
choices.feedback: أَنْتَ means 'you'. You are talking about yourself: أَنَا شَبْعَان (I'm full).

npc.ar: لَا، لَا! أَنْتَ نَحِيف جِدًّا. كُلْ، كُلْ!
npc.en: No, no! You're far too thin. Eat, eat!

choices.ar: حَاضِر يَا دُكْتُورَة! قِطْعَة صَغِيرَة فَقَطْ، مِنْ فَضْلِكِ.
choices.en: All right, doctor! Just a small piece, please.
choices.feedback: Good: accepting a little is polite. قِطْعَة is feminine, so 'small' is صَغِيرَة.

choices.ar: حَاضِر يَا دُكْتُورَة! قِطْعَة صَغِير فَقَطْ، مِنْ فَضْلِكِ.
choices.en: All right, doctor! Just a small piece, please. (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: قِطْعَة is feminine, so the adjective takes ة too: قِطْعَة صَغِيرَة.

npc.ar: يَا فَيْصَل، بَيْتُنَا مَفْتُوح لَكَ دَائِمًا. أَنْتَ مِنَ الْعَائِلَة الْآن.
npc.en: Faisal, our home is always open to you. You're one of the family now.

choices.ar: شُكْرًا لَكُمْ، أَنْتُمْ عَائِلَة كَرِيمَة جِدًّا.
choices.en: Thank you all, you are a very generous family.
choices.feedback: Good: لَكُمْ and أَنْتُمْ thank the whole family, and كَرِيمَة agrees with عَائِلَة (feminine).

choices.ar: شُكْرًا لَكُمْ، أَنْتَ عَائِلَة كَرِيمَة جِدًّا.
choices.en: Thank you all, you (one man) are a very generous family. (wrong word)
choices.feedback: A family is several people, so 'you' is plural: أَنْتُمْ عَائِلَة كَرِيمَة جِدًّا.

npc.ar: مَسَاءُ الْخَيْر، مَكْتَبُ الْمَفْقُودَات. كَيْفَ أُسَاعِدُكَ؟
npc.en: Good evening, lost property office. How can I help you?

choices.ar: مَسَاءُ النُّور. نَسِيتُ حَقِيبَتِي فِي قِطَارِ الْإِسْكَنْدَرِيَّة، وَلَمْ أَجِدْهَا.
choices.en: Good evening. I left my bag on the train from Alexandria, and I couldn't find it.
choices.feedback: Good: after لَمْ the verb loses its final -u, so lam ajid-hā (أَجِدْهَا).

choices.ar: مَسَاءُ النُّور. نَسِيتُ حَقِيبَتِي فِي قِطَارِ الْإِسْكَنْدَرِيَّة، وَلَمْ أَجِدُهَا.
choices.en: Good evening. I left my bag on the train from Alexandria, and I couldn't find it. (wrong ending)
segs: I find it (f; ordinary present form)
choices.feedback: After لَمْ the verb loses its final -u: لَمْ أَجِدْهَا (lam ajid-hā), not lam ajidu-hā.

npc.ar: مَتَى وَصَلَ الْقِطَار؟ وَفِي أَيِّ عَرَبَة جَلَسْتَ؟
npc.en: When did the train arrive? And which carriage did you sit in?

choices.ar: وَصَلَ فِي السَّاعَة التَّاسِعَة مَسَاءً. جَلَسْتُ فِي الْعَرَبَة رَقْم أَرْبَعَة.
choices.en: It arrived at nine in the evening. I sat in carriage number four.
choices.feedback: Good: you answer both questions, and her جَلَسْتَ (you sat) becomes your جَلَسْتُ (I sat).

choices.ar: وَصَلَ فِي السَّاعَة التَّاسِعَة مَسَاءً. جَلَسْتَ فِي الْعَرَبَة رَقْم أَرْبَعَة.
choices.en: It arrived at nine in the evening. You sat in carriage number four. (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: جَلَسْتَ (-ta) means 'you sat'. For 'I sat' the ending is -tu: جَلَسْتُ.

npc.ar: وَلِمَاذَا لَمْ تَأْخُذِ الْحَقِيبَة مَعَكَ؟ هَلْ نِمْتَ فِي الْقِطَار؟
npc.en: And why didn't you take the bag with you? Did you fall asleep on the train?

choices.ar: نَعَم، نِمْتُ قَلِيلًا، وَبَعْدَ أَنْ وَصَلْنَا خَرَجْتُ بِسُرْعَة مَعَ صَدِيقِي.
choices.en: Yes, I slept a little, and after we arrived I got off in a hurry with my friend.
segs: I went out, I got off
choices.feedback: Good: نَعَم answers 'did you fall asleep?', and the rest explains why you forgot the bag.

choices.ar: لَا، نِمْتُ قَلِيلًا.
choices.en: No, I slept a little.
choices.feedback: لَا (no) and then 'I slept' contradict each other. You did fall asleep: نَعَم، نِمْتُ قَلِيلًا.

npc.ar: مَا لَوْنُ الْحَقِيبَة؟ وَمَاذَا كَانَ فِيهَا؟
npc.en: What colour is the bag? And what was in it?

choices.ar: هِيَ حَقِيبَة زَرْقَاء صَغِيرَة. كَانَ فِيهَا كِتَاب وَكَامِيرَا وَمِفْتَاحُ شَقَّتِي.
choices.en: It's a small blue bag. There was a book in it, a camera and the key to my flat.
choices.feedback: Good: both answers at once. حَقِيبَة is feminine, so the colour is زَرْقَاء and 'small' is صَغِيرَة.

choices.ar: هِيَ حَقِيبَة زَرْقَاء صَغِيرَة.
choices.en: It's a small blue bag.
choices.feedback: Good: the colour first, in the feminine زَرْقَاء to agree with حَقِيبَة. She will ask about the contents next.

choices.ar: هِيَ حَقِيبَة أَزْرَق صَغِيرَة.
choices.en: It's a small blue bag. (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: أَزْرَق is the masculine. حَقِيبَة is feminine, so the colour is feminine too: حَقِيبَة زَرْقَاء.

npc.ar: وَمَاذَا كَانَ فِيهَا؟
npc.en: And what was in it?

choices.ar: كَانَ فِيهَا كِتَاب وَكَامِيرَا وَمِفْتَاحُ شَقَّتِي.
choices.en: There was a book in it, a camera and the key to my flat.
choices.feedback: Good: كَانَ فِيهَا (there was in it) uses her own words, with -hā for the bag.

choices.ar: كَانَ فِيهِ كِتَاب وَكَامِيرَا وَمِفْتَاحُ شَقَّتِي.
choices.en: There was a book in it, a camera and the key to my flat. (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: فِيهِ (-hi) points to a masculine word. The bag, حَقِيبَة, is feminine: كَانَ فِيهَا.

npc.ar: أَنْتَ مَحْظُوظ! وَجَدُوا حَقِيبَة زَرْقَاء فِي الْعَرَبَة رَقْم أَرْبَعَة. هَلْ هٰذِهِ حَقِيبَتُكَ؟
npc.en: You're lucky! They found a blue bag in carriage number four. Is this your bag?

choices.ar: نَعَم، هٰذِهِ هِيَ! الْحَمْدُ لِلّٰه! شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا.
choices.en: Yes, that's the one! Thank God! Thank you very much.
choices.feedback: Good: هٰذِهِ هِيَ (this is it) is feminine because it stands for حَقِيبَة.

choices.ar: نَعَم، هٰذَا هُوَ! الْحَمْدُ لِلّٰه! شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا.
choices.en: Yes, that's the one! Thank God! Thank you very much. (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: هٰذَا هُوَ is masculine, but you mean the bag, حَقِيبَة, which is feminine: هٰذِهِ هِيَ.

choices.ar: نَعَم، هٰذِهِ هِيَ! شُكْرًا لَكَ.
choices.en: Yes, that's the one! Thank you. (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: لَكَ (-ka) is for a man. The clerk is a woman: شُكْرًا لَكِ (-ki), or simply شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا.

npc.ar: أَهْلًا يَا فَيْصَل! كَيْفَ كَانَتْ عُطْلَتُكَ؟ أَيْنَ ذَهَبْتَ؟
npc.en: Hi, Faisal! How was your holiday? Where did you go?

choices.ar: كَانَتْ رَائِعَةً! سَافَرْتُ مَعَ صَدِيقِي إِلَى الْأُقْصُر وَأَسْوَان.
choices.en: It was wonderful! I travelled to Luxor and Aswan with my friend.
choices.feedback: Good: عُطْلَة is feminine, so كَانَتْ رَائِعَةً, with -an after 'was'.

choices.ar: كَانَ رَائِعًا! سَافَرْتُ مَعَ صَدِيقِي إِلَى الْأُقْصُر وَأَسْوَان.
choices.en: It was wonderful! I travelled to Luxor and Aswan with my friend. (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: 'It' is the holiday, عُطْلَة, which is feminine: كَانَتْ رَائِعَةً.

npc.ar: وَمَاذَا فَعَلْتُمَا فِي الْأُقْصُر؟
npc.en: And what did you two do in Luxor?

choices.ar: زُرْنَا الْمَعَابِد الْقَدِيمَة، وَفِي الصَّبَاح الْبَاكِر رَكِبْنَا مُنْطَادًا فَوْقَ النِّيل.
choices.en: We visited the ancient temples, and early in the morning we went up in a balloon over the Nile.
choices.feedback: Good: she asks 'you two' (-tumā), and you answer with 'we' (-nā): زُرْنَا، رَكِبْنَا.

choices.ar: زُرْتُمَا الْمَعَابِد الْقَدِيمَة.
choices.en: You two visited the ancient temples. (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: زُرْتُمَا means 'you two visited'. You and your friend are 'we': زُرْنَا الْمَعَابِد الْقَدِيمَة.

npc.ar: يَا سَلَام! وَهَلْ كَانَ الْجَوُّ حَارًّا هُنَاكَ؟
npc.en: Wow! And was the weather hot there?

choices.ar: كَانَ حَارًّا فِي النَّهَار، لٰكِنَّهُ كَانَ لَطِيفًا فِي الْمَسَاء. وَأَنْتِ؟ لَمْ تَذْهَبِي إِلَى أَيِّ مَكَان؟
choices.en: It was hot in the daytime, but it was pleasant in the evening. And you? Didn't you go anywhere?
segs: you go (to a woman; form after 'lam')
choices.feedback: Good: after لَمْ, تَذْهَبِينَ loses its -na: لَمْ تَذْهَبِي. And you turn the question back to Maryam.

choices.ar: كَانَ حَارًّا فِي النَّهَار، لٰكِنَّهُ كَانَ لَطِيفًا فِي الْمَسَاء. وَأَنْتِ يَا مَرْيَم؟ أَيْنَ ذَهَبْتِ؟
choices.en: It was hot in the daytime, but it was pleasant in the evening. And you, Maryam? Where did you go?
choices.feedback: Good: الْجَوّ is masculine (كَانَ حَارًّا), and ذَهَبْتِ (-ti) asks a woman where she went.

choices.ar: كَانَتْ حَارَّةً فِي النَّهَار.
choices.en: It was hot in the daytime. (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: 'It' is الْجَوّ (the weather), which is masculine: كَانَ حَارًّا فِي النَّهَار.

npc.ar: لَا، لَمْ أُسَافِرْ. زَارَنَا أَقَارِبِي مِنَ الْإِسْكَنْدَرِيَّة، وَهُمْ بَقُوا عِنْدَنَا أُسْبُوعًا كَامِلًا.
npc.en: No, I didn't travel. My relatives from Alexandria visited us, and they stayed with us for a whole week.

choices.ar: وَهَلْ خَرَجْتُمْ مَعًا يَا مَرْيَم؟
choices.en: And did you all go out together, Maryam?
choices.feedback: Good: Maryam and her relatives are several people, so 'you went out' is خَرَجْتُمْ (-tum).

choices.ar: وَهَلْ خَرَجْتِ مَعًا يَا مَرْيَم؟
choices.en: And did you (one woman) go out together, Maryam? (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: مَعًا (together) needs more than one person. You mean Maryam and her relatives: خَرَجْتُمْ مَعًا.

npc.ar: لَمْ أُسَافِرْ. زَارَنَا أَقَارِبِي مِنَ الْإِسْكَنْدَرِيَّة، وَهُمْ بَقُوا عِنْدَنَا أُسْبُوعًا كَامِلًا.
npc.en: I didn't travel. My relatives from Alexandria visited us, and they stayed with us for a whole week.

choices.ar: وَهَلْ خَرَجْتُمْ مَعًا يَا مَرْيَم؟
choices.en: And did you all go out together, Maryam?
choices.feedback: Good: Maryam and her relatives are several people, so 'you went out' is خَرَجْتُمْ (-tum).

choices.ar: وَهَلْ خَرَجْتَ مَعَهُمْ يَا مَرْيَم؟
choices.en: And did you go out with them, Maryam? (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: خَرَجْتَ (-ta) is for a man. To Maryam say خَرَجْتِ (-ti), or ask about them all: وَهَلْ خَرَجْتُمْ مَعًا؟

npc.ar: نَعَم، ذَهَبْنَا إِلَى الْأَهْرَام. لٰكِنْ أَخِي لَمْ يَذْهَبْ مَعَنَا، لِأَنَّهُ كَانَ مَرِيضًا.
npc.en: Yes, we went to the pyramids. But my brother didn't come with us, because he was ill.

choices.ar: سَلَامَتُهُ! أَرْجُو أَنْ يَكُونَ بِخَيْر الْآنَ.
choices.en: I'm sorry he was ill! I hope he is well now.
choices.feedback: Good: سَلَامَتُهُ is the polite wish for someone who is ill, with -hu for her brother.

choices.ar: سَلَامَتُهَا! أَرْجُو أَنْ تَكُونَ بِخَيْر الْآنَ.
choices.en: May she get well! I hope she is well now. (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: Her brother was ill, so use 'he' forms: سَلَامَتُهُ! أَرْجُو أَنْ يَكُونَ بِخَيْر الْآنَ.

npc.ar: تَفَضَّلِي، اِجْلِسِي هُنَا. مِمَّ تَشْكِينَ؟
npc.en: Please come in and sit here. What seems to be the problem?

choices.ar: يُؤْلِمُنِي حَلْقِي كَثِيرًا، وَعِنْدِي حَرَارَة مُنْذُ يَوْمَيْنِ.
choices.en: My throat hurts a lot, and I have had a temperature for two days.
choices.feedback: Good: حَلْق (throat) is masculine, so the verb starts with yu-: يُؤْلِمُنِي حَلْقِي.

choices.ar: تُؤْلِمُنِي حَلْقِي كَثِيرًا، وَعِنْدِي حَرَارَة مُنْذُ يَوْمَيْنِ.
choices.en: My throat hurts a lot, and I have had a temperature for two days. (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: حَلْق (throat) is masculine, so the verb starts with yu-, not tu-: يُؤْلِمُنِي حَلْقِي.

npc.ar: هَلْ عِنْدَكِ سُعَال أَوْ صُدَاع أَيْضًا؟
npc.en: Do you also have a cough or a headache?

choices.ar: عِنْدِي صُدَاع فِي الْمَسَاء، لٰكِنْ لَيْسَ عِنْدِي سُعَال.
choices.en: I have a headache in the evening, but I don't have a cough.
choices.feedback: Good: his عِنْدَكِ (you have) becomes your عِنْدِي (I have), and لَيْسَ عِنْدِي says what you don't have.

choices.ar: عِنْدَكِ صُدَاع فِي الْمَسَاء، لٰكِنْ لَيْسَ عِنْدَكِ سُعَال.
choices.en: You have a headache in the evening, but you don't have a cough. (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: عِنْدَكِ means 'you have'; you copied the question. About yourself say عِنْدِي: عِنْدِي صُدَاع … لَيْسَ عِنْدِي سُعَال.

npc.ar: طَيِّب. اِفْتَحِي فَمَكِ، مِنْ فَضْلِكِ… حَلْقُكِ أَحْمَر جِدًّا.
npc.en: OK. Open your mouth, please… Your throat is very red.

choices.ar: هَلْ هٰذَا خَطِير يَا دُكْتُور؟
choices.en: Is it serious, doctor?
choices.feedback: Good: هَلْ starts a yes/no question, and يَا دُكْتُور is the usual way to address a doctor.

choices.ar: هَلْ يَجِبُ أَنْ آخُذَ دَوَاءً؟
choices.en: Do I have to take any medicine?
choices.feedback: Good: after أَنْ the verb ends in -a (آخُذَ), and دَوَاءً takes -an as the object.

choices.ar: هَلْ هٰذَا خَطِيرَة يَا دُكْتُور؟
choices.en: Is it serious, doctor? (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: هٰذَا is masculine, so the adjective has no ة: هَلْ هٰذَا خَطِير؟

npc.ar: لَا، لَا تَقْلَقِي. حَلْقُكِ مُلْتَهِب فَقَطْ، وَهٰذَا لَيْسَ خَطِيرًا.
npc.en: No, don't worry. Your throat is just inflamed, and that isn't serious.

choices.ar: هَلْ يَجِبُ أَنْ آخُذَ دَوَاءً؟
choices.en: Do I have to take any medicine?
choices.feedback: Good: after أَنْ the verb ends in -a (آخُذَ), and دَوَاءً takes -an as the object.

choices.ar: هَلْ يَجِبُ أَنْ آخُذُ دَوَاءً؟
choices.en: Do I have to take any medicine? (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: After أَنْ the verb ends in -a, not -u: أَنْ آخُذَ.

npc.ar: نَعَم، هٰذِهِ وَصْفَة: حَبَّة مَرَّتَيْنِ فِي الْيَوْم، خَمْسَةَ أَيَّام.
npc.en: Yes, here is a prescription: one tablet twice a day for five days.

choices.ar: شُكْرًا يَا دُكْتُور. حَبَّة مَرَّتَيْنِ فِي الْيَوْم، خَمْسَةَ أَيَّام.
choices.en: Thank you, doctor. One tablet twice a day, for five days.
choices.feedback: Good: repeating the dose back is a sensible way to check you understood it.

choices.ar: شُكْرًا يَا دُكْتُورَة. حَبَّة مَرَّتَيْنِ فِي الْيَوْم، خَمْسَةَ أَيَّام.
choices.en: Thank you, doctor (to a woman). One tablet twice a day, for five days. (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: دُكْتُورَة is a woman doctor. This doctor is a man: يَا دُكْتُور.

npc.ar: وَلَا تَشْرَبِي مَشْرُوبَات بَارِدَة، وَارْتَاحِي فِي الْبَيْت.
npc.en: And don't drink cold drinks, and rest at home.

choices.ar: شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا يَا دُكْتُور، مَعَ السَّلَامَة.
choices.en: Thank you very much, doctor. Goodbye.
choices.feedback: Good: شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا and مَعَ السَّلَامَة close the visit politely.

choices.ar: أَهْلًا وَسَهْلًا يَا دُكْتُور.
choices.en: Welcome, doctor.
choices.feedback: أَهْلًا وَسَهْلًا greets someone who arrives. You are leaving, so thank him and say goodbye: شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا يَا دُكْتُور، مَعَ السَّلَامَة.

npc.ar: صَبَاحُ الْخَيْر! كَيْفَ أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أُسَاعِدَكَ؟
npc.en: Good morning! How can I help you?

choices.ar: صَبَاحُ النُّور. أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَشْتَرِيَ دَوَاءً لِلسُّعَال لِأُخْتِي الصَّغِيرَة.
choices.en: Good morning. I want to buy some cough medicine for my little sister.
choices.feedback: Good: أَنْ joins the two verbs, and the second one ends in -a: أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَشْتَرِيَ.

choices.ar: صَبَاحُ النُّور. أُرِيدُ أَشْتَرِي دَوَاءً لِلسُّعَال لِأُخْتِي الصَّغِيرَة.
choices.en: Good morning. I want to buy some cough medicine for my little sister. (wrong form)
choices.feedback: Join the two verbs with أَنْ, and the second verb ends in -a: أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَشْتَرِيَ دَوَاءً.

npc.ar: كَمْ عُمْرُهَا؟ وَهَلْ عِنْدَهَا حَرَارَة؟
npc.en: How old is she? And does she have a temperature?

choices.ar: عُمْرُهَا سِتّ سَنَوَات، وَلَيْسَ عِنْدَهَا حَرَارَة، الْحَمْدُ لِلّٰه.
choices.en: She is six years old, and she doesn't have a temperature, thank God.
choices.feedback: Good: -hā (her) all through, and سِتّ has no ة because سَنَة (year) is feminine.

choices.ar: عُمْرُهُ سِتّ سَنَوَات، وَلَيْسَ عِنْدَهُ حَرَارَة، الْحَمْدُ لِلّٰه.
choices.en: He is six years old, and he doesn't have a temperature, thank God. (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: -hu means 'his'. You are talking about your sister: عُمْرُهَا … عِنْدَهَا (-hā).

npc.ar: إِذًا هٰذَا الشَّرَاب جَيِّد لِلْأَطْفَال، وَهُوَ بِطَعْمِ الْفَرَاوِلَة.
npc.en: Then this syrup is good for children, and it tastes of strawberry.

choices.ar: مُمْتَاز! نُور تُحِبُّ الْفَرَاوِلَة. كَمْ مَرَّةً فِي الْيَوْم؟
choices.en: Excellent! Nour loves strawberries. How many times a day?
choices.feedback: Good: تُحِبُّ (ta-) for Nour, a girl, and after كَمْ the noun is singular with -an: كَمْ مَرَّةً.

choices.ar: مُمْتَاز! نُور يُحِبُّ الْفَرَاوِلَة. كَمْ مَرَّةً فِي الْيَوْم؟
choices.en: Excellent! Nour loves strawberries. How many times a day? (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: يُحِبُّ (yu-) is 'he loves'. Nour is a girl: نُور تُحِبُّ (tu-).

npc.ar: مِلْعَقَة صَغِيرَة ثَلَاثَ مَرَّات فِي الْيَوْم، بَعْدَ الْأَكْل.
npc.en: One small spoonful three times a day, after food.

choices.ar: فَهِمْتُ. وَهَلْ تَبِيعُونَ مَنَادِيل وَعَسَلًا أَيْضًا؟
choices.en: I see. And do you sell tissues and honey too?
choices.feedback: Good: تَبِيعُونَ (you sell, plural) asks about the whole pharmacy, not one person.

choices.ar: فَهِمْتُ. كَمِ الْحِسَاب، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ؟
choices.en: I see. How much is that, please?
choices.feedback: Good: before al- the sukūn of كَمْ becomes i, كَمِ الْحِسَاب, and -ka is right for the pharmacist.

choices.ar: فَهِمْتُ. كَمِ الْحِسَاب، مِنْ فَضْلِكِ؟
choices.en: I see. How much is that, please? (to a woman)
choices.feedback: مِنْ فَضْلِكِ (-ki) is for a woman. The pharmacist is a man: مِنْ فَضْلِكَ (-ka).

npc.ar: الْمَنَادِيل هُنَاكَ، لٰكِنْ لَيْسَ عِنْدَنَا عَسَل، آسِف.
npc.en: The tissues are over there, but we don't have any honey, sorry.

choices.ar: لَا مُشْكِلَة. كَمِ الْحِسَاب، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ؟
choices.en: No problem. How much is that, please?
choices.feedback: Good: لَا مُشْكِلَة answers his 'sorry', then you ask for the bill politely.

choices.ar: شُكْرًا، اللّٰهُ يُسَلِّمُكَ.
choices.en: Thanks, God keep you safe.
choices.feedback: اللّٰهُ يُسَلِّمُكَ answers a get-well wish like سَلَامَتُهَا. Here he says sorry, so answer لَا مُشْكِلَة.

npc.ar: خَمْسَة وَأَرْبَعُونَ جُنَيْهًا. سَلَامَتُهَا!
npc.en: Forty-five pounds. I hope she gets well soon!
segs: (wishing) her safety: 'get well soon' (about a woman)

choices.ar: شُكْرًا، اللّٰهُ يُسَلِّمُكَ. مَعَ السَّلَامَة!
choices.en: Thanks, God keep you safe. Goodbye!
choices.feedback: Good: اللّٰهُ يُسَلِّمُكَ is the set answer to سَلَامَتُهَا, with -ka for the pharmacist.

choices.ar: شُكْرًا، اللّٰهُ يُسَلِّمُكِ. مَعَ السَّلَامَة!
choices.en: Thanks, God keep you safe (to a woman). Goodbye! (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: يُسَلِّمُكِ (-ki) is for a woman. The pharmacist is a man: اللّٰهُ يُسَلِّمُكَ (-ka).

npc.ar: مَسَاءُ الْخَيْر يَا فَيْصَل! أَنَا جَارَتُكَ سُعَاد، مِنَ الطَّابِق الثَّالِث.
npc.en: Good evening, Faisal! I'm your neighbour Suad, from the third floor.
segs: your neighbour (a woman; to a man)

choices.ar: مَسَاءُ النُّور يَا سَيِّدَة سُعَاد! تَفَضَّلِي، كَيْفَ أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أُسَاعِدَكِ؟
choices.en: Good evening, Mrs Suad! Please come in. How can I help you?
segs: I help you (to a woman, after an)
choices.feedback: Good: تَفَضَّلِي and أُسَاعِدَكِ both end in the -i of a woman.

choices.ar: مَسَاءُ النُّور يَا سَيِّدَة سُعَاد! تَفَضَّلْ، كَيْفَ أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أُسَاعِدَكِ؟
choices.en: Good evening, Mrs Suad! Please come in (to a man). How can I help you? (wrong ending)
segs: I help you (to a woman, after an)
choices.feedback: تَفَضَّلْ is said to a man. To Mrs Suad say تَفَضَّلِي.

npc.ar: شُكْرًا، لَنْ أَدْخُلَ. جِئْتُ لِأَدْعُوَكَ إِلَى حَفْلَةِ عِيدِ مِيلَادِ وَلَدِي آدَم يَوْمَ السَّبْت.
npc.en: Thank you, I won't come in. I've come to invite you to my son Adam's birthday party on Saturday.

choices.ar: شُكْرًا عَلَى الدَّعْوَة! كُلُّ عَامٍ وَهُوَ بِخَيْر. كَمْ عُمْرُهُ الْآنَ؟
choices.en: Thank you for the invitation! Happy birthday to him. How old is he now?
segs: well ('kullu ʿāmin wa-huwa bi-khayr': happy birthday to him)
choices.feedback: Good: كُلُّ عَامٍ وَهُوَ بِخَيْر wishes Adam a happy birthday, and عُمْرُهُ (his age) asks about him.

choices.ar: شُكْرًا عَلَى الدَّعْوَة! كُلُّ عَامٍ وَهُوَ بِخَيْر. كَمْ عُمْرُهَا الْآنَ؟
choices.en: Thank you for the invitation! Happy birthday to him. How old is she now? (wrong ending)
segs: well ('kullu ʿāmin wa-huwa bi-khayr': happy birthday to him)
choices.feedback: عُمْرُهَا means 'her age'. Adam is a boy: كَمْ عُمْرُهُ الْآنَ؟

npc.ar: سَيَكُونُ عُمْرُهُ سِتَّ سَنَوَات. الْحَفْلَة فِي الْحَدِيقَة أَمَامَ الْبِنَايَة، فِي السَّاعَة الْخَامِسَة.
npc.en: He'll be six years old. The party is in the garden in front of the building, at five o'clock.

choices.ar: يَوْمَ السَّبْت فِي السَّاعَة الْخَامِسَة؟ لَا مُشْكِلَة، لَنْ أَكُونَ مَشْغُولًا. سَآتِي بِكُلِّ سُرُور.
choices.en: Saturday at five? No problem, I won't be busy. I'll come with pleasure.
choices.feedback: Good: the future negative is لَنْ + the verb in -a (لَنْ أَكُونَ), and مَشْغُولًا takes -an after 'be'.

choices.ar: لَا مُشْكِلَة، لَا سَأَكُونُ مَشْغُولًا. سَآتِي بِكُلِّ سُرُور.
choices.en: No problem, I won't be busy. I'll come with pleasure. (wrong form)
choices.feedback: Arabic never puts لَا before sa-. The future negative is لَنْ + the verb in -a: لَنْ أَكُونَ مَشْغُولًا.

npc.ar: رَائِع! سَيَكُونُ هُنَاكَ أَطْفَال كَثِيرُونَ مِنَ الْبِنَايَة، وَكَعْكَة كَبِيرَة طَبْعًا.
npc.en: Wonderful! There will be lots of children from the building, and a big cake of course.

choices.ar: هَلْ أُحْضِرُ شَيْئًا؟ أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَشْتَرِيَ هَدِيَّة لِآدَم. مَاذَا يُحِبُّ؟
choices.en: Shall I bring something? I'd like to buy a present for Adam. What does he like?
choices.feedback: Good: asking what the child likes is a kind way to choose a present, and يُحِبُّ (yu-) is about Adam.

choices.ar: سَأَذْهَبُ إِلَى السُّوق غَدًا لِأَشْتَرِيَ هَدِيَّة لِآدَم.
choices.en: I'll go to the market tomorrow to buy a present for Adam.
choices.feedback: Good: after لِ (in order to) the verb ends in -a: لِأَشْتَرِيَ.

choices.ar: هَلْ أُحْضِرُ شَيْئًا؟ أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَشْتَرِيَ هَدِيَّة لِآدَم. مَاذَا تُحِبِّينَ؟
choices.en: Shall I bring something? I'd like to buy a present for Adam. What do you like? (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: تُحِبِّينَ asks what Suad likes. The present is for Adam: مَاذَا يُحِبُّ؟ (what does he like?)

npc.ar: هُوَ يُحِبُّ كُرَةَ الْقَدَم كَثِيرًا، لٰكِنْ لَا تَشْتَرِ شَيْئًا غَالِيًا، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ!
npc.en: He loves football, but please don't buy anything expensive!

choices.ar: إِذًا سَأَذْهَبُ إِلَى السُّوق غَدًا لِأَشْتَرِيَ لَهُ كُرَة صَغِيرَة.
choices.en: Then I'll go to the market tomorrow to buy him a small ball.
choices.feedback: Good: a small ball is cheap and fits what he likes. كُرَة is feminine, so صَغِيرَة.

choices.ar: إِذًا سَأَذْهَبُ إِلَى السُّوق غَدًا لِأَشْتَرِيَ لَهُ كُرَة صَغِير.
choices.en: Then I'll go to the market tomorrow to buy him a small ball. (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: كُرَة is feminine, so the adjective takes ة too: كُرَة صَغِيرَة.

npc.ar: فِكْرَة جَمِيلَة! سَيَفْرَحُ كَثِيرًا. إِذًا نَرَاكَ يَوْمَ السَّبْت.
npc.en: What a lovely idea! He'll be very happy. So we'll see you on Saturday.

choices.ar: إِنْ شَاءَ اللّٰه. شُكْرًا مَرَّةً أُخْرَى، وَمَعَ السَّلَامَة يَا سَيِّدَة سُعَاد!
choices.en: God willing. Thank you again, and goodbye, Mrs Suad!
choices.feedback: Good: إِنْ شَاءَ اللّٰه is the usual answer to a plan for the future.

choices.ar: إِنْ شَاءَ اللّٰه. شُكْرًا مَرَّةً أُخْرَى، وَمَعَ السَّلَامَة يَا سَيِّد سُعَاد!
choices.en: God willing. Thank you again, and goodbye, Mr Suad! (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: سَيِّد is 'Mr'. Suad is a woman: يَا سَيِّدَة سُعَاد.

npc.ar: يَا فَيْصَل، مَا رَأْيُكَ؟ نِهَايَةَ الْأُسْبُوع الْقَادِم سَنَذْهَبُ إِلَى الْبَحْر فِي الْعَيْن السُّخْنَة!
npc.en: Faisal, what do you think? Next weekend we'll go to the sea at Ain Sokhna!
segs: Ain (part of the place name; lit. the spring)
Sokhna (Ain Sokhna: a beach town on the Red Sea)

choices.ar: فِكْرَة رَائِعَة! لٰكِنْ فِي نُوفَمْبِر، هَلْ سَيَكُونُ الْجَوّ دَافِئًا عَلَى الْبَحْر؟
choices.en: A great idea! But in November, will the weather be warm by the sea?
choices.feedback: Good: فِكْرَة is feminine (رَائِعَة), and after سَيَكُونُ the description takes -an: دَافِئًا.

choices.ar: فِكْرَة رَائِع! لٰكِنْ فِي نُوفَمْبِر، هَلْ سَيَكُونُ الْجَوّ دَافِئًا عَلَى الْبَحْر؟
choices.en: A great idea! But in November, will the weather be warm by the sea? (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: فِكْرَة is feminine, so the adjective takes ة too: فِكْرَة رَائِعَة.

npc.ar: عَادَةً نَعَم، فَالْبَحْر الْأَحْمَر دَافِئ فِي الْخَرِيف. لٰكِنْ سَأَنْظُرُ إِلَى نَشْرَةِ الطَّقْس فِي هَاتِفِي أَوَّلًا.
npc.en: Usually, yes: the Red Sea is warm in autumn. But I'll look at the weather forecast on my phone first.

choices.ar: حَسَنًا. كَيْفَ سَيَكُونُ الطَّقْس يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَة؟
choices.en: All right. What will the weather be like on Friday?
choices.feedback: Good: كَيْفَ سَيَكُونُ الطَّقْس؟ is the standard way to ask about the forecast.

choices.ar: حَسَنًا. كَيْفَ سَيَكُونُ الطَّقْس يَوْمَ السَّبْت؟
choices.en: All right. What will the weather be like on Saturday?
choices.feedback: Good: Saturday instead of Friday. يَوْمَ (on the day of) ends in -a because it says when.

choices.ar: حَسَنًا. أَيْنَ سَيَكُونُ الطَّقْس يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَة؟
choices.en: All right. Where will the weather be on Friday? (wrong question word)
choices.feedback: أَيْنَ means 'where'. To ask what the weather will be like, use كَيْفَ: كَيْفَ سَيَكُونُ الطَّقْس؟

npc.ar: يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَة سَتَكُونُ هُنَاكَ رِيَاح قَوِيَّة، وَرُبَّمَا تُمْطِرُ قَلِيلًا. هٰذَا غَرِيب فِي مِصْر!
npc.en: On Friday there will be strong winds, and it might rain a little. That's strange in Egypt!

choices.ar: رِيَاح وَمَطَر؟ إِذًا لَنْ نَسْبَحَ يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَة. وَيَوْمَ السَّبْت؟
choices.en: Wind and rain? Then we won't swim on Friday. And what about Saturday?
choices.feedback: Good: the future negative is لَنْ + the verb in -a: لَنْ نَسْبَحَ.

choices.ar: رِيَاح وَمَطَر؟ إِذًا لَا سَنَسْبَحُ يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَة.
choices.en: Wind and rain? Then we won't swim on Friday. (wrong form)
choices.feedback: The future negative is لَنْ + the verb in -a, never لَا + sa-: لَنْ نَسْبَحَ يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَة.

npc.ar: يَوْمَ السَّبْت سَيَكُونُ الْجَوّ مُشْمِسًا وَدَافِئًا، وَدَرَجَةُ الْحَرَارَة سِتٌّ وَعِشْرُونَ.
npc.en: On Saturday it will be sunny and warm, and the temperature will be twenty-six degrees.

choices.ar: مُمْتَاز! إِذًا سَنَذْهَبُ يَوْمَ السَّبْت. مَتَى سَنَخْرُجُ مِنَ الْقَاهِرَة؟
choices.en: Excellent! So we'll go on Saturday. When will we leave Cairo?
segs: we will go out, we will leave
choices.feedback: Good: sa- + the present makes the future: سَنَذْهَبُ، سَنَخْرُجُ.

choices.ar: مُمْتَاز! إِذًا سَنَذْهَبُ يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَة.
choices.en: Excellent! So we'll go on Friday.
choices.feedback: Friday will be windy and rainy. Saturday is the sunny day: سَنَذْهَبُ يَوْمَ السَّبْت.

npc.ar: سَنَخْرُجُ فِي السَّاعَة السَّادِسَة صَبَاحًا لِنَصِلَ قَبْلَ الظُّهْر، فَالطَّرِيق طَوِيل.
npc.en: We'll leave at six in the morning so that we arrive before noon, because the road is long.
segs: we will go out, we will leave

choices.ar: وَمَاذَا نَأْخُذُ مَعَنَا؟ أَنَا لَا أَعْرِفُ الْبَحْر الْأَحْمَر.
choices.en: And what should we take with us? I don't know the Red Sea at all.
choices.feedback: Good: لَا + the present says 'not' now: لَا أَعْرِفُ (I don't know).

choices.ar: وَمَاذَا نَأْخُذُ مَعَنَا؟ أَنَا لَا أَعْرِفُ الْبَحْر الْحَمْرَاء.
choices.en: And what should we take with us? I don't know the Red Sea at all. (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: بَحْر is masculine, so the colour is masculine too: الْبَحْر الْأَحْمَر.

npc.ar: خُذْ قُبَّعَةً وَمَاءً كَثِيرًا، لِأَنَّ الشَّمْس قَوِيَّة هُنَاكَ. وَخُذْ مِعْطَفًا خَفِيفًا لِلْمَسَاء.
npc.en: Take a hat and lots of water, because the sun is strong there. And take a light jacket for the evening.

choices.ar: اِتَّفَقْنَا! سَأَشْتَرِي قُبَّعَة جَدِيدَة غَدًا. لَنْ أَنْسَى الْمَاء هٰذِهِ الْمَرَّة!
choices.en: Agreed! I'll buy a new hat tomorrow. I won't forget the water this time!
choices.feedback: Good: قُبَّعَة is feminine, so جَدِيدَة, and لَنْ أَنْسَى is the future negative.

choices.ar: اِتَّفَقْنَا! سَأَشْتَرِي قُبَّعَة جَدِيد غَدًا.
choices.en: Agreed! I'll buy a new hat tomorrow. (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: قُبَّعَة is feminine, so the adjective takes ة too: قُبَّعَة جَدِيدَة.

npc.ar: مَسَاءُ الْخَيْر! إِلَى أَيْنَ تُسَافِرُ الْيَوْمَ؟ جَوَازُ السَّفَر وَالتَّذْكِرَة، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ.
npc.en: Good evening! Where are you flying to today? Your passport and ticket, please.

choices.ar: مَسَاءُ النُّور. أُسَافِرُ إِلَى الْقَاهِرَة. تَفَضَّلْ، هٰذَا جَوَازُ سَفَرِي.
choices.en: Good evening. I'm flying to Cairo. Here you are, this is my passport.
choices.feedback: Good: his تُسَافِرُ (you travel) becomes your أُسَافِرُ (I travel), and تَفَضَّلْ hands the passport to a man.

choices.ar: مَسَاءُ النُّور. أُسَافِرُ إِلَى الْقَاهِرَة. تَفَضَّلِي، هٰذَا جَوَازُ سَفَرِي.
choices.en: Good evening. I'm flying to Cairo. Here you are (to a woman), this is my passport. (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: تَفَضَّلِي is said to a woman. The clerk is a man: تَفَضَّلْ.

npc.ar: شُكْرًا. ضَعْ حَقِيبَتَكَ عَلَى الْمِيزَان، لَوْ سَمَحْتَ… وَزْنُهَا ثَلَاثُونَ كِيلُو!
npc.en: Thank you. Put your suitcase on the scales, please… It weighs thirty kilos!
segs: your bag, your suitcase (to a man)

choices.ar: ثَلَاثُونَ؟! هَلْ هٰذَا أَكْثَرُ مِنَ الْمَسْمُوح؟ فِيهَا هَدَايَا كَثِيرَة لِأَصْدِقَائِي فِي الْقَاهِرَة.
choices.en: Thirty?! Is that more than is allowed? There are lots of presents in it for my friends in Cairo.
choices.feedback: Good: هَدَايَا is a plural of things, so its adjective is feminine singular: هَدَايَا كَثِيرَة.

choices.ar: ثَلَاثُونَ؟! هَلْ هٰذَا أَكْثَرُ مِنَ الْمَسْمُوح؟ فِيهَا هَدَايَا كَثِير لِأَصْدِقَائِي فِي الْقَاهِرَة.
choices.en: Thirty?! Is that more than is allowed? There are lots of presents in it for my friends in Cairo. (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: A plural of things takes a feminine singular adjective: هَدَايَا كَثِيرَة, not كَثِير.

npc.ar: نَعَم، الْمَسْمُوح ثَلَاثَة وَعِشْرُونَ كِيلُو فَقَطْ. يَجِبُ أَنْ تَدْفَعَ عَنْ كُلِّ كِيلُو زِيَادَة.
npc.en: Yes, the limit is only twenty-three kilos. You have to pay for every extra kilo.

choices.ar: كَمْ أَدْفَعُ؟ وَهَلْ مِنَ الْمُمْكِن أَنْ آخُذَ بَعْضَ الْأَشْيَاء مَعِي فِي حَقِيبَةِ الْيَد؟
choices.en: How much do I pay? And is it possible to take some things with me in my hand luggage?
choices.feedback: Good: هَلْ مِنَ الْمُمْكِن أَنْ …؟ is a polite way to ask, and after أَنْ the verb ends in -a: آخُذَ.

choices.ar: كَمْ أَدْفَعُ؟ وَهَلْ مِنَ الْمُمْكِن أَنْ آخُذُ بَعْضَ الْأَشْيَاء مَعِي فِي حَقِيبَةِ الْيَد؟
choices.en: How much do I pay? And is it possible to take some things with me in my hand luggage? (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: After أَنْ the verb ends in -a, not -u: أَنْ آخُذَ.

npc.ar: مُمْكِن. حَقِيبَةُ الْيَد حَتَّى سَبْعَة كِيلُو. أَوْ تَدْفَعُ عَشَرَةَ دَنَانِير عَنْ كُلِّ كِيلُو.
npc.en: It's possible. Hand luggage can be up to seven kilos. Or you pay ten dinars for every kilo.

choices.ar: عَشَرَةُ دَنَانِير لِكُلِّ كِيلُو؟ هٰذَا أَغْلَى مِنَ الْهَدَايَا! لَحْظَة، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ.
choices.en: Ten dinars a kilo? That's more expensive than the presents! One moment, please.
choices.feedback: Good: 'more expensive than' is أَغْلَى مِنْ, and لَحْظَة، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ asks politely for a moment.

choices.ar: أَخَذْتُ الْكُتُب وَالْكُوفِيَّة مِنَ الْحَقِيبَة. هَلْ وَزْنُهَا الْآنَ أَقَلُّ؟
choices.en: I've taken the books and the keffiyeh out of the suitcase. Does it weigh less now?
choices.feedback: Good: you move things into your hand luggage at once. وَزْنُهَا uses -hā because حَقِيبَة is feminine.

choices.ar: عَشَرَةُ دَنَانِير لِكُلِّ كِيلُو؟ هٰذَا غَالٍ مِنَ الْهَدَايَا!
choices.en: Ten dinars a kilo? That's expensive from the presents! (wrong form)
choices.feedback: غَالٍ (expensive) does not compare. 'More expensive than' is أَغْلَى مِنْ: هٰذَا أَغْلَى مِنَ الْهَدَايَا.

npc.ar: طَبْعًا، تَفَضَّلْ.
npc.en: Of course, go ahead.

choices.ar: أَخَذْتُ الْكُتُب وَالْكُوفِيَّة مِنَ الْحَقِيبَة. هَلْ وَزْنُهَا الْآنَ أَقَلُّ؟
choices.en: I've taken the books and the keffiyeh out of the suitcase. Does it weigh less now?
choices.feedback: Good: أَخَذْتُ (-tu) is 'I took', and أَقَلُّ (less) is the comparative of قَلِيل.

choices.ar: أَخَذْتَ الْكُتُب وَالْكُوفِيَّة مِنَ الْحَقِيبَة. هَلْ وَزْنُهَا الْآنَ أَقَلُّ؟
choices.en: You've taken the books and the keffiyeh out of the suitcase. Does it weigh less now? (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: أَخَذْتَ (-ta) means 'you took'. You did it yourself: أَخَذْتُ (-tu).

npc.ar: نَعَم، الْآنَ ثَلَاثَة وَعِشْرُونَ كِيلُو بِالضَّبْط. مُمْتَاز! تَفَضَّلْ، هٰذِهِ بِطَاقَةُ الصُّعُود.
npc.en: Yes, now it's exactly twenty-three kilos. Excellent! Here you are, this is your boarding pass.

choices.ar: شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا! مَعَ السَّلَامَة.
choices.en: Thank you very much! Goodbye.
choices.feedback: Good: شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا and مَعَ السَّلَامَة, and you keep your presents without paying extra.

choices.ar: شُكْرًا لَكِ! مَعَ السَّلَامَة.
choices.en: Thank you (to a woman)! Goodbye. (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: لَكِ (-ki) is for a woman. The clerk is a man: شُكْرًا لَكَ (-ka), or شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا.
